text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- United States: One quarter of homes in Jewish settlements are empty; Administration officials to defence minister - when flats empty, no need to expand settlements.
- Confidential report to Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai: army is partly responsible for those who evade military service.

- British intelligence documents on World War Two Nazi Holocaust: "Final Solution" began in June 1941, not in early 1942; Seven million Jews were killed, not six as previously thought; Allies knew of extermination campaign in early stage.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu mulling diplomatic changes: Aide Dore Gold as ambassador to Washington, present ambassador Eliahu Ben Elissar to United Nations.
- Without public transportation system, Israel's highway network will have to be enlarged sevenfold by year 2020.
- Woman murders her retarded daughter, then hangs herself.
- Ross won't return as long as sides ignore his efforts to push talks forward.
- Visiting Greek FM: joint naval exercises with Israel in summer.
JERUSALEM POST
- Ambassador to Washington Eliahu Ben-Elissar returns home to fight for his job.
- Suicide attack on navy boat fails.
- British documents indicate: seven million Jews died in Holocaust.
- Mother strangles daughter, hangs self.
- Soccer star Ronnen Harazi arrested on tax evasion charges.
- Elias Freij resigns as Bethlehem mayor, Palestinian tourism minister.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu rejects U.S.-formulated compromise on curbing Jewish settlement building; dispute with Washington deepens.
- Gunboat sailors foil attempted seaborne suicide attack.
- Ben-Elissar arrives for urgent visit to discuss his future in job.
- Rare step: Defendant charged with murder held in house arrest.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Ben-Elissar: "Netanyahu will not take me out of here by force." Ambassador enraged by Netanyahu's intention to replace him with aide Dore Gold.
- United States: Despite difficulties in Israeli-Palestinian talks, we will continue to mediate.
- p. 13. FBI agents and Russian minister aiding in investigating mafia.
GLOBES
- Israel GDP grew at 2.8 percent annualised rate
